page: Microsoft Azure L48as_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture and managed by Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is equipped with an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor delivering 48 dedicated vCPUs across 24 physical cores clocked at up to 3.7 GHz. Hardware vector instructions include AVX, AVX-512, and AVX512 VNNI alongside hardware cryptographic extensions. The instance is configured with 384 GB of system RAM, providing an 8 GB per vCPU allocation, and includes 11,519 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage. There are no discrete GPU accelerators integrated into this server type.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong computational and caching throughput. Stress-ng scores reached 3,078.56 on single-core and 73,818.26 on multi-core runs, corroborated by a Geekbench multi-core rating of 19,783.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 62,728.2. Cached memory bandwidth for small blocks clocked at 3,646.79 GB/sec, while in-memory operations showed exceptional capability with Redis achieving 70.18 million SET operations per second. However, uncached 256 MB memory transfers settled around 111.65 GB/sec read and 82.84 GB/sec write. In natural language workloads, large-model execution shows sharp throughput decay, registering 2.53 tokens per second on 70B parameter text generation due to the absence of dedicated tensor processing hardware.

With its dense configuration of local NVMe storage and balanced memory capacity, the L48as_v4 provides high resource density for I/O-intensive workloads without incurring external disk attachment overheads. Tradeoffs center on the high baseline footprint and lack of public IPv4 addresses, requiring dedicated routing architectures. This instance is best aligned with large-scale relational and NoSQL database clusters, real-time distributed data caching, big data ingestion, and heavy multi-threaded data compression tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure L48as_v4 is a storage-optimized instance engineered for I/O-demanding and data-dense enterprise workloads. Driven by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor, the system provides 48 dedicated vCPUs across 24 physical cores at 3.7 GHz, paired with 384 GB of memory and 11,519 GB of integrated NVMe SSD local storage. Benchmark testing highlights top-tier multi-threaded processing power, evidenced by a PassMark CPU score of 62,728.2, alongside exceptional in-memory key-value performance reaching 70.18 million Redis SET operations per second. While unaccelerated large model inference is limited by the absence of discrete GPUs, the server delivers balanced memory bandwidth and fast local I/O. Its configuration delivers cost-effective density for storage-bound operations by bundling massive local NVMe capacity directly with substantial memory. The L48as_v4 is particularly well fitted for distributed NoSQL databases, transactional engines, caching layers, and high-throughput data processing pipelines.
